subject: Multi-region Dedicated: commits, throughput credits, and DR packaging
messages:
From: Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@pivotalai.com
Date: 2026-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the overview last week. Before we pull procurement in, a few clarifying questions on Dedicated multi-region pricing and how committed capacity/credits work across regions:

1) Do we need to reserve separate GPU pools per region (us-east & eu-west) or can a single committed pool be shared across regions for billing/commit purposes?
2) If we replicate for DR (active-passive copies in a standby region), are we charged for both pools as full committed capacity?
3) How do burst/throughput credits apply — are they per-pool or pooled across a tenant?
4) Any flexibility to allocate a single annual commit across regions dynamically if our traffic shifts?

We're evaluating two packaging options: (A) smaller per-region commits to limit upfront spend but higher per-token cost; (B) larger unified commit with a cross-region allocation mechanism. Pivotal is sensitive to double-paying for standby capacity but needs low RTO.

Can you share concrete pricing examples with numbers (GPU counts, baseline throughput, typical discounts) and outline what DR options we should consider? I can loop in our contracts lead if it makes sense.

Thanks,
Andre Silva\VP of ML Platform\Pivotal AI

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>, contracts@pivotalai.com
Date: 2026-09-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Andre — great questions. High level answers upfront, followed by a short worked example and next steps.

Summary answers:
- Separate committed pools are the default (per-region pools) for predictability and isolation. However we offer an allocation layer for reserved commits in select enterprise deals that lets you flex commitments across regions within a billing construct.
- Standby/replicated pools are charged based on the reserved capacity you commit to them. For active-passive DR where the standby is kept warm but not serving steady traffic, we can offer a reduced-rate standby factor (typically 30-50% of full commit) as part of negotiated packaging.
- Throughput/burst credits are normally applied per-pool, but with an enterprise allocation add-on they can be aggregated and consumed from a shared credit bucket.
- Yes — dynamic allocation across regions is possible with a cross-region commit policy (requires a contractual addendum and minimum commit size).

Worked example (proposal):
- Baseline: you need ~8 A100-equivalent GPUs in Primary (us-east) for steady throughput ~ 5k tokens/sec overall. EU usage: ~2 A100-equivalent steady.
- Option A (per-region commits): 8 GPUs (us-east) + 2 GPUs (eu-west) committed. Price = (8 * $Xk/mo) + (2 * $Xk/mo). No cross-region flexibility.
- Option B (unified commit with allocation): 10 GPUs committed at a slightly lower unit price (10% discount on per-GPU list) and an allocation policy that allows shifting up to 30% of the commit between regions monthly. Includes a shared burst credit pool (100k tokens/day) and 1:1 failover SLA for 30-minute RTO.
- DR standby: if you want an active-passive replica in EU kept warm, we can offer standby at 40% of full commit cost if the standby is configured as passive (no KV cache warm-up) and you accept an 8-hour warm-up window. For fast failover (under 30 minutes) standby price is ~70% of full commit because we maintain warm caches and pre-warmed kernels.

I'll pull in Dev (SE) and Karthik (pricing) to add concrete numbers and a packaged XLSX. If acceptable, we can prepare a commercial term sheet and a short addendum for cross-region allocation.

Best,
Rishi\Account Executive, Redwood Inference\rishi@redwood.com

From: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Thanks — adding technical constraints and sizing notes so pricing aligns with expected throughput and failover behavior.

Key technical points:
- GPU equivalence: Our pricing maps to an A100-80GB baseline. If you require different hardware (H100 or smaller GPUs), we translate equivalents.
- Throughput guarantees: We commit per-pool sustained tokens/sec for a configured request size distribution. Example SLA: 5k tokens/sec sustained across the 8-GPU pool (95th percentile) with burst headroom of +20% for short periods.
- Cache/replication cost drivers: Warm standby requires periodic KV cache snapshots and a small replication traffic pattern; this increases network egress and memory usage and is the main reason for standby pricing.
- Autoscaling & burst: Dedicated pools can be configured with burst capacity (shared spare GPUs) — billing for burst is based on usage minutes at a higher unit price.

Operational recommendation:
- If RTO < 30 minutes is mandatory: plan for a warm standby in-region EU at ~70% cost of full commit.
- If you can accept 4–12 hour warm-up: standby at ~30–50% cost is reasonable.
- If traffic shifts significantly seasonally, unified commit with allocation is best; if traffic is stable and critical, per-region commits minimize cross-region contention.

I can attach an annotated sizing worksheet (I filled in approximate p95 token/sec and estimated cache sizes).

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Andre — following up with concrete pricing bands and an initial commercial package you can review. Attached: RI_Dedicated_MultiRegion_PRICING_v2.xlsx and SLA-DR-Options.pdf.

Commercial summary (list prices rounded for example):
- Unit: 1x A100-equivalent GPU reserved
- List price (per GPU / month): $18,000
- Volume discounts: 10% @ 10 GPUs, 18% @ 30 GPUs, 25% @ 60+ GPUs (applies to committed GPUs across the contract)
- Standby discounts: Warm standby 70% of unit price for <30 min RTO; 40% for 4–12 hour warm-up
- Cross-region allocation add-on: available with minimum 12 GPU commit; add-on fee = $1,200/mo + 4% uplift on committed spend for the allocation control plane
- Burst capacity: billed at 1.8x unit price for minutes consumed; pools include a small daily token credit (20k tokens) by default

Example (your baseline):
- Option A total: 8 GPUs * $18k * (1 - 0.10) = $129,600/mo (US) + 2 GPUs * $18k * (1 - 0.00) = $36,000/mo (EU) => $165,600/mo total (no cross-region flexibility)
- Option B unified commit 10 GPUs with 10% discount: 10 * $18k * (1 - 0.10) = $162,000/mo + cross-region add-on $1,200/mo + 4% uplift on committed spend = $6,480/mo => effective $169,680/mo but includes allocation + shared credits + better unit economics when usage shifts.

Promotional concession: For Pivotal AI we can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of first-year committed spend and extend the 10% discount tier to kicks in at 8 GPUs instead of 10, subject to exec approval.

Next steps: if Pivotal confirms which option they prefer, we can produce a redlineable term sheet and route to finance for the promo concession.

—Karthik
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

From: Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@pivotalai.com, dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-06T08:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful. A few follow-up/clarification points from our procurement side:

- Can the 8->10 GPU threshold for the 10% discount (as proposed in the promo concession) be made explicit in the term sheet? Procurement needs a clear trigger.
- For standby pricing: we want the 40% standby option but with a maximum warm-up of 8 hours. Can Redwood commit to a documented warm-up plan (steps + expected cache rehydrate time)?
- Cross-region allocation add-on: can you confirm whether burst credits consumed in one region reduce the shared pool for the other (i.e., are they truly global)?

If you can confirm those in a short addendum, I can get contracts to review. Assuming we get the 8-GPU trigger and the 40% standby with 8-hour warm-up, we are likely to proceed with Option B and the allocation add-on.

Regards,
Andre

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Andre Silva <andre@pivotalai.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, contracts@pivotalai.com
Date: 2026-09-08T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated multi-region commit & DR questions

Andre — confirmed and next steps.

1) Discount trigger: we will state explicitly in the term sheet that an 8-GPU committed baseline (across regions) unlocks the 10% unit discount for the term. That will be captured in the commercial summary table.
2) Standby warm-up: Dev will produce a two-page warm-up and cache rehydrate plan that commits to an <=8 hour warm-up for the configuration we've discussed (KV snapshot frequency, pre-warmed kernels, and a failover choreography). Ill attach that as an addendum to the SLA.
3) Shared burst credits: confirmed — with the allocation add-on, burst credits are global to the tenant (consumption in one region reduces the shared global pool). We'll document token accounting rules (UTC daily reset, overflow handling).

Commercial proposal: Option B (10 GPU unified commit) with:
- 10 GPUs @ 10% discount (triggered at 8 GPU baseline per the promo)
- Cross-region allocation add-on enabled ($1,200/mo + 4% uplift)
- Warm standby in EU (40% standby cost, 8-hour warm-up)
- One-time onboarding credit = 5% first-year committed spend
\I will prepare a short term sheet and send to contracts. If that looks good, please confirm and we'll circulate DocuSign.

Thanks — appreciate the quick coordination.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
